findings.text: System call entry for syslog accepts a numeric action plus user buffer and length and forwards to the central syslog implementation with reader origin. Size query actions return sizes or counts, unknown actions fail as invalid argument.

Unread size query with no valid record at the current cursor returns zero. A cursor that no longer matches the first valid record is repaired to that record with partial offset cleared. Proc origin yields pending record count while other origins accumulate printable sizes over remaining records, starting timestamp mode from partial state for the first record then using global mode, finally subtracting partial progress.

The unread size path serializes cursor validation and size accumulation under syslog_lock, unlocking on empty and non empty completions. Total buffer size query and invalid action handling do not acquire this mutex.
Console ownership ordering is tracked by a lock dependency map labeled for the owner, a task pointer recording the current owner, and a boolean recording waiter presence.

Recursion accounting uses per CPU normal and NMI byte counters with early byte fallbacks before per CPU data is ready. Context in NMI selects NMI storage, other contexts select normal storage, each preferring per CPU storage when ready and early storage otherwise.
Maximum print nesting depth equals three.
A mostly read integer holds a configurable per message delay in milliseconds.
Caller identifier mask equals hexadecimal 80000000, selecting the top bit.
A mostly read boolean permits messages from non panic CPUs during panic when set. An early boot option sets it and emits an informational message, always succeeding.
Variadic print service forwards caller format and arguments to the central formatted output routine and returns its character count.
Timestamp inclusion is disabled in this build, the syslog cursor is a static 64 bit sequence, and a global pointer designates the early console.

Preferred console table services allow adding entries by name and index or device name with options, marking user specified entries and remembering that at least one user entry exists, plus later binding a device name entry to a concrete driver name and index.

Addition rejects entries with neither name nor device name and rejects named entries with negative index. Existing entries matching by name and index or by device name are reused without duplication, updating preferred position unless braille options are present and preserving user specified marking. Table full is reported as too big.

Command line console option parsing maps empty or null values to the null TTY, strips braille settings, distinguishes device style values containing a separator from TTY style values, normalizes numeric TTY shorthand and legacy SPARC aliases, splits options at comma, derives index from trailing digits or leaves it negative for device style, then records the result as user specified.
Message format boot option selects syslog or default formatting based on exact keyword match and always reports handled.
Console suspend support defaults to enabled. An early boot option disables it and always reports handled.
A file local boolean records suppression of automatic verbose console behavior. No accessor or mutator appears in these fragments.

CPU hotplug notification does nothing while tasks are frozen. Otherwise it flushes nonblocking atomic pending output when that mode is active and performs a lock then unlock cycle to flush legacy direct output when that mode is active, always reporting success.
Query service reports whether the legacy console lock is currently held.
Shared print buffers are provided as a single global instance of the print buffers aggregate for use when per context buffers are unavailable.

Console TTY lookup acquires the console lock, walks consoles under SRCU read protection skipping entries without a device callback, returns the first driver and index produced, then releases SRCU and the console lock.

Suspend service first flushes the target console with a bounded wait, then clears its enabled flag under list lock and waits for SRCU readers so no other context can still observe it enabled before the caller suspends the underlying port.

Resume service sets the enabled flag under list lock, waits for SRCU readers so printing contexts observe enabled state, wakes the appropriate offload mechanism based on console kind and active flush modes, then flushes with a bounded wait.

Console list mutations hold the list lock while flag updates use the SRCU flag writer. Readers walk under SRCU read lock with cookie protection. Mutations that remove or reposition entries or toggle enabled state issue an SRCU synchronization before reuse so prior walks have completed.

Legacy printer thread wake predicate returns true when stop is requested. Otherwise it skips nonblocking consoles that can print via atomic or offload paths, skips unusable consoles, compares each remaining console sequence against ring validity using per console sequence for legacy and shared sequence reader for nonblocking, waking when any valid pending record exists. Thread pointer and ready flag track lifecycle with read only after init protection for readiness.

Legacy printer thread alternates between interruptible wait on its wait queue and a locked flush loop. Each flush iteration checks stop, takes the console lock, flushes one record learning next sequence plus handover and retry indications, and unlocks unless handover occurred. Retry repeats without sleeping, otherwise control returns to waiting.

Shutdown path under list lock clears the running flag once, stops per console nonblocking threads, then performs an atomic flush of leftover backlog. Syscore registration binds this shutdown callback and a late init step registers syscore, marks threads ready, and triggers a locked readiness check.
A mostly read integer retains boot consoles when set. An early boot option sets it, logs a debug note, and always reports handled.

Preferred promotion requires the target already registered and does nothing when it is already first. Otherwise it detaches the entry without reinitializing linkage so registration checks still succeed, synchronizes SRCU, marks the new head as console device with a device callback expectation, clears that marking from the prior head via SRCU flag writer, and inserts the target at the head.

Console enabled state moves from enabled to disabled on suspend and back on resume, each transition serialized by list lock with SRCU grace ensuring observers converge before port suspension or before printing resumes, bracketed by bounded flushes.

Early console initialization installs the null TTY as default when no command line console was given and that default is configured, initializes the default TTY discipline, then invokes each registered console initcall in order with tracing of level start and per call result.

Late print initialization under list lock unregisters boot consoles whose control block or callbacks reside in init memory, then installs CPU hotplug callbacks for dead and online transitions with warnings on failure, and initializes print sysctls.
Sysctl initialization registers the print control table under the kernel directory during early init.
Pending print flags equal one for wakeup and two for output.

Per CPU pending state combines output and wakeup bits and is atomically exchanged to zero by lazy interrupt work. Output handling wakes the legacy thread when forced to thread mode and that thread exists, otherwise attempts legacy lock flush. Wakeup handling wakes log waiters. Work is declared as lazy per CPU interrupt work.

Flush trigger fans out to atomic flush, offload thread wake, direct legacy lock flush, and deferred legacy output according to active flush modes. Deferred formatted services emit with scheduler context level and no caller device, with variadic wrapper forwarding to the va list form.
Rate limit query forwards caller function name to the shared print rate limit state and returns its decision.

Timed rate limiter compares current jiffies against caller stored timestamp, suppressing when a prior timestamp exists and elapsed time is within the requested millisecond interval, otherwise updating the timestamp and permitting.
Dumper list updates hold the dump list spinlock with interrupts saved and restored. Unregister additionally waits for RCU grace after list removal so concurrent readers complete.

Dumper registration requires a dump callback, rejects duplicate registration as busy, and appends to the dump list with tail RCU semantics on success. Unregister rejects entries not registered as invalid, otherwise clears registration and removes with RCU semantics.
A file local boolean controls unconditional kmsg dumping. No accessor appears in these fragments.
Dump reason translator maps panic, oops, emergency and shutdown reasons to fixed display names and returns unknown for other values.

Dump buffer retrieval clamps an old cursor to the minimum retained sequence, repairs to first valid sequence when records were lost, and stops when cursor has reached the iterator end. It selects the oldest starting sequence whose records fit the supplied capacity accounting for terminator, then formats records in order advancing through the buffer and moves the iterator end to the chosen start so later calls walk older blocks, reporting output length and success.

Replay service attempts the console lock without blocking, rewinds all consoles on success, triggers pending flushes according to active modes including deferred output, then unlocks which flushes consoles.

Per system print CPU ownership uses an atomic owner holding CPU number or negative one for free plus an atomic nesting count. Ownership query compares owner to current CPU, wait spins with relaxation until free, and try acquisition uses acquire compare exchange succeeding when free or reentrant on same CPU with nesting increment, otherwise failing without blocking.

Preferred console entries observed here carry a name field and a device name field plus a short index, an options pointer, and a user specified flag. Matching uses name with index or device name alone, and binding fills name and index from driver values.

Consoles observed here carry name and index with flags and sequence state, linkage for list membership, and callbacks for device lookup plus write read and unblank with private data. Flags distinguish boot, enabled, console device and nonblocking kinds.
Dump clients observed here provide a dump callback and carry a registered flag with list linkage for RCU membership. Iteration state carries current and next sequence cursors used to bound retrieval.

Deep print recursion beyond three risks overflow without the byte counters and early fallbacks. Stale syslog and dump cursors after record loss must be repaired to first valid sequence, otherwise callers would observe gaps or block on vanished records.

Boot consoles referencing init memory after init would fault if not unregistered. Toggling enabled state or repositioning list entries without SRCU grace would let concurrent walks use a suspended port or observe torn linkage.

Dump formatting must reserve terminator space and reject null or zero length buffers to avoid overrun. Lost wakeups are avoided by combining output and wakeup bits in per CPU state with atomic exchange and by rechecking stop and validity under appropriate locks.
